checked_sources.evidence: Directly opened. IAU table separately lists Horologium/Hor, Hydrus/Hyi, and Hydra/Hya.

Directly opened. Explicitly places NGC 1512 in Horologium; supports barred spiral, 70,000-light-year diameter, 2,400-light-year central circumnuclear starburst ring, gas funneling along bar. Caption says 30 million light-years; object metadata lists 40 million.

Directly opened. Says NGC 1512 is 30 million light-years away in Horologium; image description identifies the larger dense oval of orange spiral arms beginning at bar ends. Confirms current draft separates this from central starburst ring.

Directly opened. Fast facts list Hydrus; text places the star-forming region in the SMC Wing, says NGC 602 contains at least three clusters, compares NGC 602a to Orion by age/mass/size, and describes extended X-rays likely from overlapping emission of several thousand young low-mass stars rather than hot massive-star-wind gas.
Directly opened. Object metadata identifies NGC 602 as a star-cluster grouping in Hydrus.
Directly opened. Identifies the SMC as a dwarf galaxy and Milky Way satellite; places young stars in its Wing.
